Behind the polished podcasts, he’s a relentless experimenter in relationships, always testing how kindness and curiosity can reshape habits.

education.description:
Back home where it all started.
http://www.redditblog.com/2014/11/coming-home.html

Executive chair until coming back full-time in July 2015.
Helping founders make something people love.
I help make it rain on our non-profit's bank account.
I'm writing a book for aspiring entrepreneurs eager to embrace the future of the World Wide Web for fun, profit, and for the good of humankind.
Built a brand people love.

Breadpig, Inc. was founded with the purpose of being an uncorporation. Rather than following the typical corporate directive of maximizing shareholder wealth, breadpig aims to do interesting (good) things with its profits. Don't tell our shareholders.
Invest, advise, consult and sometimes play video games.
See reddit.
Got paid to read, as well as provide impeccable customer service to all the patrons of the parking garage. Responsible for giving proper change and keeping the booth tidy.

Started as a dishwasher and got promoted to cook after my first shift. Cooked for a year and asked to serve so I could make more money. Waiting tables was a great experience because of the emphasis it places on customer service  since basically your entire income is riding on it (which is why its a good idea to tip well). Nowadays, helping a user with a bug in the code is much easier than helping a customer with one in their food.

Graduated with high distinction in History, thesis titled "Is There Nothing Intelligent to Say About a Massacre? Conflicting Contemporary Perceptions of the Bombing of Dresden." Ask me about this (or anything from 20th century European history) sometime, if you want to excite me.

Also graduated with a B.S. (yes, a B.S.) in Commerce, concentrating in management and international business -- now I'm looking for an international business to manage.

Minored in German, but this was kind of cheating since my mom is from Hamburg.

What got you here isn’t what’s going to get you to your first million.

If you’re new here, hi! I’m Amy Porterfield 👋

I’ve been in business for 17 years, and in that time, so much has changed. This year, I changed my entire business model to focus on one thing: coaching female founders.

Why? Because when I was trying to grow from half a million to a million, I desperately needed a coach and a mentor. Someone who had already been where I was going. And that support is what helped me get from my first million all the way to $139M.

A woman needs another woman who has gone before her to help her make those big pivots. Someone who can see what’s getting in the way

Not everyone in your corner can tell you what’s holding your business back 👀

My overarching mission is to empower people to make choices in life from a point of awareness, not ignorance.

Over the past 18 years in the internet and technology space, I’ve had the privilege of working on several ventures - founding some, investing in others, and learning from all. 

Over 16 million people follow my work across social platforms, where I share my experiences and insights on career, mindset, startups, personal finance, and relationships.

Today, my main focus is building my 3 startups

1/ WebVeda.com
A growth platform, offering skills, community and jobs at an annual subscription. 
WebVeda has over 500,000 members as of May 2026

2/ India Genius Challenge
Nation-wide search for the brightest kids in India, through a 2-phase program. 
Winners of the IGC get a Rs. 10L scholarship towards their higher education. 

3/ Monzy.co
The place to find YOUR best credit card.
No ads. No sponsorships. No personal data sought or tracked. 

I’ve also written six bestselling books that have sold 1Mn+ copies worldwide across 63 countries and translated into 17 languages:
- Do Epic Shit (2022)
- Get Epic Shit Done (2023)
- Make Epic Money (2024)
- Build An Epic Career (2025)
- Beyond The Syllabus (2025): for teenagers only
- Winning People Without Losing Yourself (2026)

It’s been a journey shaped more by reflection and exploration than certainty, and I wouldn’t have it any other way.

IGC comprises of 5-min daily online challenges (completely free of cost) where school kids earn Genius Points (GPs) and compete with kids across the country. 
Daily, Weekly, Monthly National winners get books, smartwatches, earphones, iPads, laptops. 

The top performers in the online challenges will be invited to the National Finals in Delhi, where the winner of IGC will win Rs. 10L of scholarship.

posts.caption: Everybody is jealous of the destination. Nobody is jealous of the journey.

5 money rules my wife and I follow as a couple aged 45 with two kids.

1. We don’t spend money to look rich. 

We spend to become wealthy and gain freedom of our time.

So, there’s no car. It’s rented. 
We own the house we live in, no other real estate.

No spending on brands. No spending just to show off to people.

2. We spend extravagantly on high-quality food.

We know that what goes into our body is ultimately the biggest wealth we have, and unfortunately, healthy food is not cheap.

3. We spend on experiences more than things.

Things give you happiness once, and they have no end.

You r

Before you say yes to marriage, check these 5 things.

1. Why are you getting married? Is it for the sake of society? Is it for the sake of your parents? Is it for your own good?

2. How do you handle fights with your partner? Because fights will continue. If you handle them properly, then relationships will progress.

3. Do you have an alignment on money and responsibility? How will you spend money? How will you share responsibilities?

4. Do you have space for your own personality? You can make friends without involving their friends. You can live your own life without depending on them.

5.

4 signs that your life is much better than you think.

1/ Someone in your family has stopped worrying about you - because they trust you now.

2/ Your 18-year-old self wouldn't believe where you've reached.

3/ People now ask you for advice about something you once used to panic about.

4/ One bad day doesn't ruin your entire week, one bad week doesn't ruin your month, and one bad month doesn't ruin your year.

Sometimes, you've already made more progress than you realise.

There's a difference we often miss.

Being dependent means you need them to function. 
Being dependable means they can count on you, and you on them, without either of you losing yourselves.

One comes from fear. 
The other comes from strength.

The strongest relationships aren't two people who can't live without each other.

They're two whole people who choose, every day, to be someone the other can rely on.

3 reasons we bought our first home at 40 and not at 25 or 30.

1/ By the time we hit 40, we knew we wanted to live in Delhi.

At 25 or 30, there’s so much flexibility in life to change cities, even change countries if you want to.

But by the time we reached 40, we already knew we’re going to stay here. That’s why we chose this place.

2/ At that time, we had enough money that we could afford its EMI and its down payment for the house we wanted to live in.

At 25 or 30, that house wasn’t affordable for us.

3/ The house we wanted to live in is a very premium apartment.

Should you tell your parents how much you earn?

There’s a case for yes. They raised you, supported you, and may have every reason to know.

But there’s another side.

Once they know your salary, expectations can change - a bigger house, a car, a trip, a higher contribution at home.

So instead of telling them exactly how much you earn, you could tell them what your money can do for them.

“I can contribute ₹X towards the house.”

“I can afford this trip.”

“I can cover this EMI.”

Tell them what your money can do, not necessarily how much you make.

A counterpoint of view - do you agree?

Some people don't add to your life. 
They slowly drain it.

The ones who confuse you. 
The ones who hurt you and call it a joke. 
The ones who take your energy and give nothing back.

We keep them around out of guilt, or history, or habit.

But protecting your peace isn't cold. 
It's necessary.

You're allowed to walk away from anyone who only knows how to take.

5 questions people ask - and how we hear them.

1/ “When are you getting married?”

We hear that nothing I’ve done in life so far means nothing until I get married.

2/ “How much do you earn now?”

We hear that my entire worth is based on one salary, one number, and that will give me a rank.

3/ “Sharma ji’s son, well…”

We hear that I will never be enough. Someone else will always be doing better than me.

4/ “You studied so much and you’re doing this?”

We hear that if I make my own choices in life, that will never be accepted.

When a child is punished for the truth, they don’t stop doing the thing.

They just get better at hiding it.

Fear doesn’t build honesty. 
It builds distance. 
It teaches a child that the safest option is to never let you see who they really are.

The kids who grow up telling their parents the truth aren’t the ones who were scared into it.They’re the ones who knew the truth was safe.

This will be a slightly controversial take.

Living in Mumbai on ₹1 lakh a month, or at your home, your village, your city, ₹60,000 a month.

Many people will say the financially right decision is to stay at your home. 
There’s no rent, work-life balance is much better, and expenses are lower.

linkedin.about:
I’m the founder and CEO of Thrive Global, a behavior change technology company with the mission of improving health and helping us move from merely surviving to thriving. I also founded The Huffington Post and have written 15 books, including Thrive and The Sleep Revolution.

I’m originally from Greece (and still have the accent to prove it!). When I was 17, I moved to England and studied economics at Cambridge University, where I frankly spent most of my time debating at the Cambridge Union.

I live in New York but also spend time in Los Angeles, and love being a Yiayia (Greek for grandmother) to my almost three-year-old grandson Alexander and his newborn sister Annabel.

My journey to focusing on health began with a fall. In April 2007, I collapsed from exhaustion and burnout and hit my head on my desk on the way down, breaking my cheekbone.
 
In the wake of my fall, I found myself going from doctor to doctor to find out what was wrong. Doctors’ waiting rooms were good places for me to ask myself a lot of questions about the kind of life I was living.

After all the tests, it turned out nothing was wrong. Except for the fact that everything was wrong. I was suffering from an acute case of burnout. I had bought into the myth that burnout was the price I had to pay for success. 

I became more and more passionate about the five daily habits that drive so much of our health: nutrition, exercise, sleep, stress management and connection. That led me to write Thrive and The Sleep Revolution. 

The books struck a chord, but I wanted to go beyond speaking and writing to helping people move from awareness to action. So in 2016 I founded Thrive Global, which helps people transform their health by combining Microsteps — small, science-backed daily steps — with technology, storytelling and community. And last year, with the OpenAI Startup Fund, we launched Thrive AI Health to build an AI health coach to democratize access to health coaching.

posts.caption:
Today is World Mental Health Day. And we’ve made great progress in recent years raising awareness and opening up the conversation about mental health.

This year, I hope we take it one step further: mental health is brain health. A growing body of research shows how our brain health connects to everything from daily brain fog and anxiety to long-term cognitive decline.

So here’s a Microstep to try today: take a moment to check-in with your own mental health by naming the feeling you’re having right now in one word. Simply putting a feeling into words can help calm the brain’s stress response.

AI keeps pulling off things that used to be impossible. In my latest On My Mind newsletter, I write why we shouldn’t lose sight of the eight “wonders of life,” as coined by @UCBerkeleyOfficial professor Dacher Keltner, that create everyday moments of awe: moral beauty, movement, nature, music, visual design, spirituality and religion, big ideas, and life and death.

Plus, dispatches from @Dreamforce, the @LucasMuseum, and my own home, where I recently hosted an event that captured the possibility of this moment when it comes to brain health.

You can read my newsletter at the link in bio.

Wise words, whether we’re elite athletes competing at the highest levels or building healthy habits in our daily lives. Congrats to @CaitlinClark22 — @WNBA Comeback Player of the Year! — on a great season, and thank you for your deep commitment to helping people live healthier lives by putting a spotlight on healthy behaviors, including the role of exercise as one of the most powerful preventative medicines, and reminding us all to start how we can.

As @ariannahuff pointed out, our generation rarely talked about menopause when we were younger. But we’re shouting it from the rooftops now, because women deserve better—not only from the health care system, but from their workplaces too. #menopauseawarenessmonth 

Read more about the @gallup x @pivotaldotcom survey on women’s health at the link in my bio.

“The more we share…the more we can accelerate the shift in the culture.” Couldn’t agree more, @ariannahuff.

Thanks for a great conversation on the need to make women’s health more visible.

linkedin.about:
Barbara Corcoran’s credits include straight D’s in high school and college and 20 jobs by the time she turned 23. It was her next job that would make her one of the most successful entrepreneurs in the country: She borrowed $1,000 and quit her job as a waitress to start a tiny real estate company in New York City. Over the next 25 years Barbara would parlay that $1,000 loan into a $5 billion real estate business, building the largest and best-known brand in the business. 
 
Corcoran is the author of the best seller “Shark Tales: How I Turned $1,000 into a Billion Dollar Business!” and host of top business podcast “Business Unusual with Barbara Corcoran” and lifestyle podcast “888-Barbara.” 
 
Corcoran is a motivational and inspirational speaker. She is a frequent small business and real estate contributor on every major network. Corcoran has been an investor/Shark for the past ten seasons on ABC's four-time Emmy award wining show, Shark Tank, investing in over 80 businesses to date. Follow Barbara on Twitter and Instagram @BarbaraCorcoran.
linkedin.location: New York, New York, United States

positions.description: Get the advice you need to live a better life! From the boardroom to the bedroom, nothing’s off limits. Utterly candid and totally unfiltered, Barbara Corcoran’s got the answers. Call 888-Barbara! I'm an answering machine.

"Shark Tank" is a business reality television series by acclaimed TV producer Mark Burnett that airs on ABC Network Fridays at 8|9c. As one of the “Sharks,” Barbara Corcoran and four other prominent executives listen to business pitches from everyday people who hope to launch their company or product to new heights. Investing her own money in every deal she makes, Barbara partners with entrepreneurs and helps them turn their dreams into reality. Millions of viewers tune into the show as Barbara shares her off the cuff and brash critiques along with entrepreneurial insights and business prowess.

I'm smart at getting where I want to go. On Business Unusual I give you the straight talk and confidence you need to get there through interviews, short stories, and listener Q&A. Got a question for me? Call 888-BARBARA and I just might answer on a future episode. Listen and subscribe on Apple Podcasts or wherever you listen to podcasts.

The Barbara Corcoran Venture Partners syndicate is accessed through AngelList, a platform that gives investors access to start-up and early-stage companies. The syndicate allows investors to invest with Barbara for as little as $1,000.

Brené Brown is a research professor at the University of Houston, where she holds the Huffington Foundation Endowed Chair at the Graduate College of Social Work. She also holds the position of Professor of Practice in Management at The University of Texas at Austin McCombs School of Business.

Brené is the author of six #1 New York Times bestsellers and the host of two award-winning podcasts. Brené spends most of her time working in organizations around the world, helping develop braver leaders and more courageous cultures. In 2024, she was named Executive Chair of the Center for Daring Leadership at BetterUp. She lives in Houston, Texas, with her husband, Steve. They have two children, Ellen and Charlie, and a weird Bichon Frisé named Lucy.

posts.caption: @aclfestival is here and I get to talk to one of my favorite artists @lolayounggg. Join us on the Bonus Tracks stage tomorrow for a conversation about vulnerability, creativity, and the power of messy.

Deeply grateful to @adamgrant, our podcast team, @voxmedia, and all of you who watched and/or listened! I learned way more than I offered and for that I’m very thankful! And, last - Adam and I will be together in Dallas for the Vibe book launch later this month and taking on a fun topic in January on his pod! CAN NOT WAIT!

Thanks again, everyone!
BB❤️

When we see people attack empathy or say things like, “The fundamental weakness of Western civilization is empathy” (Elon Musk, 2025), we should ask ourselves, “What harm, pain, or hurt do they not want us to see or feel? Who do they want to hurt, humiliate, or dehumanize without accountability?”

Based on our research over the past 25 years, creating meaningful connections and human-centered systems requires a combination of compassion and cognitive empathy. I think of compassion as the daily practice and cognitive empathy as one its most powerful tools.

This is one of my favorite @thecuriosityshop episodes. In a world where everyone and everything is fighting for our attention, our rage, and our money, we exam what makes us vulnerable to persuasion and how we can develop stronger influence literacy skills. 

It’s the best kind of collision between Adam’s, “think like a scientist” research and my work on shame and vulnerability. 

Biggest finding: 
Shame around being persuadable makes us more vulnerable to influence. Acknowledging that we are vulnerable to those reels and TikTok’s and snake oil pitches makes us more resistant!

@adamgrant and I loved talking with @angelalduckworth about her new book, “Situated.”

Big takeaway:

“To stay motivated through the countless hours of practice that separate amateurs from experts, grit is necessary but not sufficient. The situation also matters—and to an astonishing degree:

Culture matters.
Mentors matter.
Teammates matter.
Even the objects in your personal space matter.

How you think about your goals and what you’re willing to do to achieve them depends on both you and your situation.”

I also loved our conversation about billboards - those signs we post around our spaces

To my Longhorn family: Try not to step in the bullshit left behind by small-minded people.
Stay strong. Like UT vs OSU strong. 🧡🤘🏻🤍

Priya Parker, one of my favorite thinkers and writers, is joining @thecuriosityshop this week and we’re talking about fighting! Not “dukes up” fighting but how real heat and conflict can build connection if we’re willing to learn how to do it well.

What I love about this conversation and Priya’s new book - “The Art of Fighting” - is being called to imagine a world where we unlearn and relearn what it means to gather and to disagree. And, she’s just so honest and fun!

To watch or listen to the full episode, head to YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

Aaron Sandel @prof.sandel, an anthropologist and primatologist, has spent over a decade studying the Ngogo chimpanzees, witnessing one of the largest known chimp communities split into two factions.

Aaron helps Adam and I understand what chimpanzees can teach us about friendship, conflict, belonging, and human nature. He shares what he learned from watching these chimps show affection, navigate dominance hierarchies, and face the effects of division within their own community.

Grateful for a mother who warned her daughters about the price she paid for trying to conform to nice girl culture in the 1950’s. We didn’t know all of the details of her wounds, but we fully understood the depth of her pain. 

When she died she had framed pictures of Gloria Steinem and Angela Davis over her desk.
 
Quote: Gloria Steinem’s remarks at the National Organization for Women’s March for the Equal Rights Amendment, Washington, D.C., July 9, 1978, as reported in James Lardner and Neil Henry, “Over 40,000 ERA Backers March,” Washington Post, July 10, 1978

📸 Warren K. Leffler

Celebrating Dolly has me thinking about the joy of reading books and how often I squander that pleasure by putting myself under pressure to consume pages. 

We are all craving deep reading, deep thinking, and deep connection — and these all require deep time. 

I went back this morning and re-read the interview we did with @mayasmarty and was drawn to her phrase the “privilege of focus.” 

Let’s start a spiritual book club where we read what we want, when we want, no meetings or deadlines - just a shared reframe of deep time as subversive in a world of shallow distraction, addictive scrolling,

Sometimes shiny is great. Sometimes it’s dangerous.

Episode available on YouTube or wherever you listen to podcasts.

From humble beginnings to a self-made multimillionaire with over $6 billion to date in global product sales and a starring role on ABC’s newest business reality TV show, Shark Tank, Daymond John is the personification of the American Dream. He continues to set standards of excellence while expanding his interests in fashion, branding, marketing, consulting, entertainment, and beyond. This industry leader, best-selling author, and ground breaking entrepreneurial expert has evolved into a highly sought after business and motivational speaker.

From his then unprecedented guerrilla marketing and branding techniques to the continuously innovative ways in which he uses social media, brand integration, and his expertise on pop culture, Daymond remains a cutting edge business strategist.

Daymond teaches audience members how to apply his successful methods to a wide range of businesses today. He shares winning tips for negotiating and negotiating for women, boosting sales, improving employee morale, increasing productivity, and optimizing staff talents.

As a motivational speaker, Daymond’s quintessential rags-to-riches success story of sacrifice, hard work, and perseverance as well as the unique and charismatic way he communicates it, will inspire any audience.

positions.description: "Shark Tank" is a business reality television series by acclaimed TV producer Mark Burnett (Survivor, The Apprentice) that airs on ABC Network. As one of the “Sharks,” Daymond John, and four other prominent executives, listen to business pitches from everyday people who hope to launch their company or product to new heights. Investing his own money in every project, Daymond John becomes partners with the entrepreneurs and helps them turn their aspirations into a reality. Millions of viewers tune into the show as John demonstrates his marketing prowess and entrepreneurial insights.

In a world saturated with marketing and advertising companies, The Shark Group distinguishes itself through non-traditional and innovative approaches in raising product awareness, while engaging the target audience and stirring emotion in consumers through entertainment.

Our integration techniques will elevate your product's status to new heights as we communicate your company's core message in a completely new fashion. We pride ourselves in strong client relationships and partnerships in order to not only meet our clients' goals, but to exceed them.

The company was founded in 1992 by Daymond John with a line of hats made in his house in Hollis, Queens, New York. According to the company website, John mortgaged his own home for $100,000 and with that seed money he and his three friends Carl Brown, J. Alexander Martin, and Keith Perrin, turned half of his house into a factory and the other half into living space.

linkedin.about:
Gary Vaynerchuk is a serial entrepreneur and serves as the Chairman of VaynerX, the CEO of VaynerMedia, and Creator and CEO of VeeFriends, and 6x New York Times Best Selling Author. Gary is considered one of the leading global minds on what's next in culture, business, and the internet. 

Known as "GaryVee," he is described as one of the most forward thinkers in business. He acutely recognizes trends and patterns early to help others understand how shifts in consumer attention impact the realities of the business world today. Gary's approach sits at the intersection of business and pop culture. He keenly understands how to bring brand relevance to the forefront. He is a prolific angel investor with early investments in companies like Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, Venmo, Snapchat, Coinbase, and Uber. 

Gary is an entrepreneur at heart – he builds businesses. Today, he helps Fortune 1000 brands leverage consumer attention through his full-service advertising agency, VaynerMedia, which has ofﬁces in Amsterdam, Bangkok, Chicago, Delhi, Kuala Lumpur, London, Los Angeles, Mexico City, Miami, New York, Tokyo, Toronto, Singapore, and Sydney. VaynerMedia is part of the VaynerX modern-day parent company, which also includes Eva Nosidam Productions, Gallery Media Group, ChukMedia, VaynerSpeakers, VaynerCommerce, Tamara Group, and Tingley Lane Trading. Gary is the Co-Founder of VaynerSports, VCR Group, VaynerWatt, Resy, and Empathy Wines. He guided Resy and Empathy to successful exits -- which he later sold to American Express and Constellation Brands, respectively. He also owns a Major League Pickleball team called the 5s, is part owner of a Big3 basketball team, and is an investor in the revival of the SlamBall League. 

Gary is also the founder and creator of VeeCon – a contemporary super conference that converges business and pop culture with innovation and technology. In addition to running multiple businesses, Gary documents his daily life as a CEO through his social media channels, which have more than 50 million followers and garner more than 2+ billion impressions per year across all platforms. His podcast, "The GaryVee Audio Experience," ranks among the top podcasts globally. 

Gary serves on the board of MikMak, Bojangles Restaurants, Global Citizen Forum, The Paley Center, and Pencils of Promise. He is also an advisor for District and a longtime Well Member of charity: water. 

Gary's life ambition is to buy the New York Jets.

positions.description:
I’m the Chairman of VaynerX, a modern-day parent company built to scale brands for the now. Our family of relevance-driving businesses includes VaynerMedia, ChukMedia, Tamara Group, Gallery Media Group, Tingley Lane Trading, and VaynerSpeakers. 

Our specialties include:

 • Creative
 • Strategy
 • Media
 • Analytics 
 • Commerce
 • Influencers
 • Experiential
 • Collectibles

Want to work with us? DM me.

VeeFriends is a contemporary entertainment company that combines art, storytelling, collecting, events and innovative technologies to build a community around a movement of kindness and positivity. The company’s mission is to scale 283 unique VeeFriends characters and their attributes to create a better world. These characters foster a sense of community and inspire creativity, self-discovery, accountability, and personal growth. VeeFriends’ characters represent qualities and traits Gary hopes to inspire in others. VeeFriends’ intellectual property was minted on the Ethereum blockchain to create unprecedented opportunities for utility, collectibility, and community building.

Vayner3 was founded to help the world’s leading enterprises navigate the next era of connected consumer behavior. Our mission is to grow your business by helping to build new markets and revolutionize digital engagement, charting a new course for enterprises. 

Vayner3 partners with leading brands to shape the next era of the internet; leverage AR, Blockchain, AI, and immersive digital experiences to future-proof your business.
Liquid Death is natural mountain water served in ice-cold infinitely recyclable cans.
VCR Group is a modern hospitality company comprised of kind and talented operators with a simple focus of creating consumer-centric experiences through unmatched hospitality.
I invested in slack pre-IPO in 2018. They were acquired in 2020 by Salesforce for $27.7B.
I invested in Twitter in 2009, a few years after it was founded.

I was an early investor in Uber in 2012 (after famously passing on it a couple of years prior). 

The company went public in 2019.
I'm an early investor in Venmo, a digital wallet that makes it easy to send & receive money.
I invested in Facebook pre-IPO in 2010, the company went public two years later.
Bojangles is a restaurant chain that started in the South, and serves food with real deal Southern flavor. I joined the board in early 2020.
Coinbase is a digital platform that makes it easier to buy & sell cryptocurrency. I invested in the company in 2014 via Vayner/RSE.
MikMak (founded by Rachel Tipograph) lets brands unify their digital storefront across online retailers. I joined the board back in 2016.

VaynerSports is a full-service athlete representation agency that guides players through a variety of issues involving their professional career. We are improving the level of service beyond what any athlete has experienced in the industry thus far, one client at a time.

I invested in Liquid IV in 2019, a wellness brand that's known for its non-GMO drink mixes. 

The company has received attention & financial backing from people including Demi Lovato, Kevin Hart, Kendall Jenner, Hailey and Justin Bieber, James Corden, Usher, DJ Khaled, Steve Aoki, Patrick Schwarzenegger, Maria Shriver, Yes Theory, Freddy Wexler, Jake Kassan, Elle and Ross Walker, and Moiz Ali.

I was an angel investor in companies like Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, Uber, and Birchbox before eventually co-founding VaynerRSE, a 25M New York-based venture capital firm specializing in seed-stage investments.

Partners include: Phil Toronto, AJ Vaynerchuk, Matt Higgins and Kerry Kellogg

Our portfolio includes: Medium, CoinBase, Birchbox, Snap, Resy, Beme, Breather, Shyp and more.

Gary co-founded VaynerMedia in 2009 with his younger brother, AJ Vaynerchuk. True to his own DNA, Gary never raised startup funding and began the business in a conference room at Buddy Media. Just nine years later, the company included more than 800 employees, servicing clients such as PepsiCo, GE, Johnson and Johnson, Chase, AbInBev and more.

Since its founding, VaynerMedia has flourished, having built best-in-class capabilities in paid media, strategy, full-service creative, influencer marketing, IoT & Voice, eCommerce, personal branding, SMB marketing and in-house consulting.

I run Winelibrary and Winelibrary.com but became more known from Winelibrarytv.com. Winelibrarytv.com is a wine video blog that ran for 1,000 episodes. I was able to taste and review 1000s of wines from all over the world.

DailyVee is a 'daily' vlog I produce which captures behind-the-scenes footage of my life as a an HR-driven CEO, entrepreneur, and public figure. 

The vlog is released daily at 12:00 EST on YouTube and Facebook. 

DailyVee captures me in meetings with employees, client pitches, and traveling the world for business.

The #AskGaryVee show is business Q&A series broadcast live on Facebook and Instagram, where I answer your questions about marketing, social media, and entrepreneurship. 

Want to get on the show? Tune in on Facebook and leave your name, number, location and phone-number or Tweet me your question with the hashtag #AskGaryVee

linkedin.about: On a mission to make people remarkable. Co-author of Think Remarkable and Wiser Guy. Host of the Remarkable People podcast. Chief evangelist of Canva.

positions.description: Guy is chief evangelist of Canva, an online graphics-design service. In this position, he "spreads the good news" about how Canva democratizes design by empowering people to create great graphics without buying or learning high-end applications.
Guy interviews remarkable people so you can be one too. For example, Jane Goodall, Margaret Atwood, Steve Wozniak, Stephen Wolfram, Martha Stewart, Arianna Huffington, and Phil Zimbardo.

positions.company: University of California, Berkeley, Haas School of Business
positions.description: Guy is an executive fellow at Haas. This means he goes to Haas several times a year and scares the crap out of the students by telling them about the real world.

education.description: Guy is on the board of directors of Cheeze. This app does one thing really well: manage albums for sharing content in a controlled manner. For example, albums for only your family, only your surfing buddies, or only your colleagues. Think of it as the anti-social social-media app.

It's a tough job, but someone has to do it. Guy is a brand ambassador for Mercedes. This means that he makes appearances for Mercedes, "unboxs" cars, and supplements Mercedes social-media efforts. And he has to drive a Mercedes all the time--yes, you read that right.

Guy was on the board of trustees of the Wikimedia Foundation. This is the entity that oversees (to the extent that anything oversees 300,000 community members!) Wikipedia and the other wiki properties. Guy serves this position because he believe the democratization of information is the third most important cause in the world--the first two being climate change and human rights.
Tripwire provides change-auditing software that ensures the security and availability of corporate networks by establishing a baseline of data in its desired state.

This was my second tour of duty at Apple. I held the position of "chief evangelist" and was an Apple fellow. My job description was to protect and preserve the Macintosh cult by doing whatever I had to do.

Fog City Software created Claris Emailer and LetterRip, two Macintosh applications. This was a great company because I got to work with three of my favorite people in the world: Will Mayall, Kathryn Henkens, and Jud Spencer.
MacUser and Macworld were competitors back then. I wrote for both of them--though not simultaneously. I simply can't remember the dates of my employment with them!
After listening to my own hype about the opportunities in Macintosh software, I left Apple to start a Macintosh database company.

My job was to convince developers to create hardware and software products for a new computer that had a zero installed base, zero backward compatibility, and zero/month sales. Towards the end of my first tour of duty at Apple, I also managed the group that published the Apple-labeled software (MacWrite, MacPaint, MacDraw, etc) that became Claris.
I will always have a soft spot in my heart for EduWare because this company enabled me to break into the tech sector from the jewelry business. I was rejected by many, many tech companies back then.

This is my first real job: counting and schlepping diamonds and fine jewelry. It is where I truly learned to sell. The jewelry business is much tougher than the computer business. Marty Gruber, my boss at Nova, had a tremendous influence on me.
I've come to believe that an MBA is a hindrance to entrepreneurship, but I do have one from UCLA. My major was marketing.

education.school: University of California, Davis - School of Law
education.description: As a good Asian-American, I went to law school to make my parents happy. Unfortunately (or maybe fortunately), I couldn't stand it and quit after two weeks. It's one of the best things that I've ever done.
These were some of the happiest days of my life. I loved Stanford. Sometimes I wish I could go back to school there. By the way, I majored in Psychology because it was the easiest major I could find.

The highest praise for the Remarkable People podcast from one of my heroes, Dr. Jane Goodall. I’m on a mission to make you remarkable with guests like Marc Benioff, Woz, Martha Stewart, Neil deGrasse Tyson, and more! Find the podcast at remarkablepeople.com or your favorite podcast player.

Charlie Euchner argues that both major political parties are failing to pay enough attention to the everyday concerns of ordinary people. 

Too much political energy, he says, gets directed toward elites and established power rather than issues like jobs, healthcare, opportunity, and community needs. 🗣️

🌱 His answer is stronger grassroots organizing that starts by listening to people and turning shared concerns into focused action. 

Tune into the latest episode of Remarkable People🎙️

Giving career advice to college students is one thing. Giving it when your son and his girlfriend are in the audience raises the stakes. This was the situation when I spoke to a group of student leaders at the University of Hawaii this Fall.

Substack link in bio 🔦

"It’s the people, stupid.” 

Charlie Euchner’s point is simple: lasting change doesn’t come from slogans, social media, or political insiders. It comes from listening to people, building relationships, and organizing around the issues that actually matter in their lives!

Don't miss his powerful episode on the Remarkable People podcast ⭐ Tune in on my YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.

What happens when you treat AI like a mad science experiment instead of just a tool? 🧪🤖 

Vivienne Ming shares how her experiments with AI revealed that the people who challenged it, pushed it, and used it to stretch their thinking could dramatically outperform both humans and AI working alone. 

Watch her full conversation on my YouTube channel!

When your calendar has no room for anything to go wrong, eventually everything might go wrong.

🏁 Subscribe to get weekly newsletters: link in bio!

Humans hate uncertainty, but Vivienne Ming points out that we are far better at navigating the unknown than anything else in existence—including cutting-edge AI. 🤖🧠 

As AI gets better at answering well-defined questions, she argues that we need to rethink what a job is and our relationship with work, putting more value on our ability to explore what we don't yet understand. 

🎧 Listen to Vivienne's full conversation with Guy Kawasaki wherever you get your podcasts.

We all have that voice of doom that tells us we’re not good enough, the idea won’t work, or we should just stop. 

Harlan Coben talks about learning to push past that voice and keep creating. ✍️🎧 

Tune into this week's episode wherever you get your podcasts 👊

At 69, she is still jumping at least once a month. 

It hasn’t been easy - and I jump with people who are in their 20’s who progress much faster than I do. But I keep pushing forward with my goals in mind.

linkedin.headline: Host of The Jamie Kern Lima Show podcast, 2x New York Times Bestselling Author, Founder, IT Cosmetics, Guest Shark on Shark Tank
linkedin.about:
Jamie Kern Lima went from Denny’s waitress to billion-dollar entrepreneur! She’s the host of the #1 Self-Improvement Podcast in the country, The Jamie Kern Lima Show podcast, where Oprah Winfrey was her first guest. She’s a Guest Shark on the upcoming Season 16 of Shark Tank on ABC. She’s a two-time New York Times bestselling author, her new book WORTHY made it 14 weeks in a row on the NY Times bestseller list. She’s founder of IT Cosmetics, a company she started in her living room and sold to L'Oréal in a billion-dollar deal, becoming the first female CEO of a brand in L’Oreal’s 100+ year history. Her love of her customers and remarkable authenticity and belief eventually landed her on the Forbes America's Richest Self-Made Women list. 

 

She's been a Denny's waitress, a struggling entrepreneur, and has overcome years of self-doubt, body-doubt and God-doubt. She's a mother of two and an active investor, speaker, and thought leader who is passionate about inspiring and elevating women. She recently held her live event called Becoming Unstoppable, where more than 260,000 women joined live from their living rooms, and many iconic women of our time including Oprah Winfrey, Ellen DeGeneres, Robin Roberts and Maria Shriver all joined to support Jamie in her mission of building self-worth in every single girl, woman and person! She's also an active philanthropist who has funded leadership training in more than 100 prisons and shelters across the US, and has donated over $40 million in product and funds to help women face the effects of cancer with confidence. She's donating 100% of her author proceeds for WORTHY. 

 

 

Jamie’s website & social media handles:

Instagram: @JamieKernLima

YouTube: @JamieKernLimaOfficial 

Facebook: @JamieKernLimaPage 

TikTok @JamieKernLimaOfficial

Especially since it’s not based only on achievement alone, but on where you started and how far you’ve come. Only in America can I go from waitressing tables (my Dennys uniform in the last photo 🥰) to launching a business with close to zero money in my living room, working hard for years and eventually building a company from that very living room that now impacts millions of people. The American Dream is possible, I’m living proof of it, i believe in it and I’m so honored to do everything I can to hel

linkedin.about: Kara Goldin is the Founder of Hint, Inc., best known for its award-winning Hint® water, the leading unsweetened flavored water. She led the company as CEO for 17 years and continues to serve on the Board. She has been named one of InStyle’s Badass 50, Fast Company’s Most Creative People in Business, Fortune’s Most Powerful Women Entrepreneurs, Fortune's Most Innovative Women in Food & Drink and EY Entrepreneur of the Year for Northern California. The Huffington Post listed her as one of six disruptors in business, alongside Steve Jobs and Mark Zuckerberg. Kara has successfully navigated the world of large companies and startups in many industries including media, tech and consumer products. In addition, she understands retail and direct to consumer well. She is an active speaker & writer and hosts the podcast The Kara Goldin Show where she interviews founders, entrepreneurs and other disruptors across various industries. Kara’s first book, Undaunted, was published by Harper Leadership in October 2020 and is now a WSJ and Amazon Best Seller. She lives in the Bay Area. Follow Kara on all social channels @KaraGoldin

posts.caption:
Happy 5th Birthday to our sweet Maggie! 🐾💕 Five years of unconditional love, endless cuddles, and so much joy. We love you, Maggie! 

#HappyBirthdayMaggie #BirthdayGirl #FiveYearsOfLove #EnglishLabLove

The Blue Angels soaring over San Francisco Bay today! 🛩️💙 

Always something spectacular to watch.

#BlueAngels #FleetWeek #SanFrancisco

Absolutely crazy to think that this week, we launched Episode 900 of The Kara Goldin Show! 🎉🎙️🎧

I couldn’t be more thrilled — or more grateful — to have had the opportunity to bring so many incredible stories to the forefront.

For those who aren’t familiar with the show, we release new episodes three days a week — Monday, Wednesday and Friday. I mostly sit down with founders, often CEOs, and sometimes people who have written a book or two along the way.

We talk about the brands they’re building — or have built — and what really happened along the way. The successes. The failures. The sur

The universe will adjust. ✨

Choose what feels right for you. ❤️

#ChooseYou #BeYou #LifeLessons
When you stop in Los Olivos on your way to Santa Barbara and run into your good friend from NYC/Santa Fe. What are the chances? ❤️ Kismet. ✨

Most of us know what we want.

We’re just really good at explaining why now isn’t the time.

More planning. More certainty. More waiting.

But waiting doesn’t close the gap. Moving does.

Take the step. 🚀

#Undaunted #KeepGoing #Life #TakeTheStep

What an incredible long weekend celebrating my nephew Pat and the beautiful newlyweds, Pat and Jackie, at their unforgettable wedding! I’m so thrilled for both of them and grateful to have witnessed such a beautiful ceremony, spent precious time with so much family, and enjoyed a great Michigan win along the way! 💙💛

This weekend was truly one for the books! Packed with unforgettable moments, so much love, nonstop fun, and plenty to be grateful for.

Feeling incredibly grateful for every single minute of it. ❤️

#WeddingWeekend #FamilyTime #MakingMemories #GratefulHeart #GoBlue @patwynne6 @j

For as long as he wants us there, for as many IKEA builds as he needs us for, we’ll always show up. 💙

One last move-in. Senior year. How did that happen so fast?

So proud. So grateful. And definitely not ready for this year to fly by.

Go @justin.goldin and Go Blue! 〽️💙

From “Orbiter” straight into “Call Your Mom” Friday night at Oracle Park.  And then the shooting star that raced through the sky. 🔥

Noah Kahan is something else. His writing. His storytelling. The way every lyric seems to hit somewhere you weren’t expecting.

I couldn’t help but think that everyone needs a Noah in their life — someone who puts words to the things the rest of us are feeling but don’t always know what to do or how to say it.  Someone who would call your mom.

Grateful to the team at Howdy.com for inviting us to join in on the fun. What a beautiful night. ❤️ Thank you @noahkaha

It’s amazing how many people take credit for what they never built—only what they were entrusted to protect.

Not nearly as many take responsibility for what happened on their watch.

And rewarding failure doesn’t turn it into success. Never does.

You can try to spin the story.

You can’t spin the scoreboard. 🔥

#RealLeadership #Accountability #ResultsMatter #Business #BrandBuilding

The truth isn’t always loud. Sometimes, it simply needs time to be seen. ⏳

I’ve learned that facts outlast narratives. The patterns and details eventually reveal themselves. Bad actors can shape the story and obscure the facts—but only for so long. Time has a way of revealing the truth… hopefully before too much damage is done.

Lessons learned. ✨

#Leadership #Entrepreneurship #Founders #LessonsLearned #Resilience

Because great brands start with people willing to try. Again and again. ✨

Always grateful for time with Karen Behnke , Founder of Juice Beauty, Inc. and now her newest venture Beauty Crush Skincare. The perspectives, honesty, and shared experiences always fill my cup.

#Entrepreneurship #Founders #Leadership #BrandBuilding #Innovation @founderkarenbehnke @juicebeauty @hint @beautycrush_skin

posts.caption:
Some words stick with you.

Over the years, I’ve collected a few quotes that genuinely changed the way I think, work, and move through life. 💭

These are a few I still come back to, because sometimes the right words at the right time can change everything.

Swipe through, and tell me: which one do you need to hear right now? 👇

Sometimes the voice telling you to quit is wisdom. Sometimes it’s fear, doubt, exhaustion, or the discomfort of doing something that actually matters. 💭

The trick is learning to tell the difference.

Before you give up, pause. Get curious. Ask yourself what’s really going on—and what you actually want.

What's something you quit that turned out to be a blessing? Tell me in the comments. 👇

Throwing it back to my conversation with Lewis Howes. 

There’s a big difference between easy money and making money easy. 💰

In my conversation with Lewis Howes, we talked about the temptation to chase the shortcut—the next big opportunity, the get-rich-quick promise, the thing that looks like easy money.

But “easy money” can come with a very expensive lesson.

Making money easy is different. It’s about building the skills, experience, and systems that make creating wealth more sustainable over time.

Want to hear the full conversation with Lewis? Comment MONEY and I’ll send you the episode

Quick question: How many sales might you have lost when the right person landed on your website, opened your email, or saw your post…
…but your words didn’t click? 😬

Great copy isn’t about sounding clever, polished, or “professional.”
It’s about knowing how to write words that connect, persuade, and sound unmistakably like YOU.

Because in a noisy world,  writing that connects is a SUPER POWER.
And the good news? It’s a skill you can learn. 🙌

Rewind to one of my favorite conversations. 💭

What if the thing you’ve been taught to see as a weakness is actually pointing you toward your greatest strength? 

In my conversation with Bryce Dallas Howard, we talked about how her learning disability shaped the way she sees herself, her strengths, and the way she works.

Sometimes the thing that makes you feel different can become the very thing that helps you find your path. ✨

Want to hear the full conversation with Bryce? Comment GIFT and I’ll send you the episode. 👇

Some weeks are full of wins.
Others are just about making it to the other side.

Whatever this week held for you, you made it through. And that counts. 🤍

Take a breath. Give yourself some credit. Now enjoy your weekend.

Happy October! 🍂🎃
There’s something about this time of year I just love. The summer travels wind down, the pace gets a little slower, and sweater weather gives me an excuse to cozy up and actually sit still for a minute. 😂

So I made myself an October bingo card with a few of my favorite fall things! 🎃👻🍁

What’s in store for you this October? 🍂

You keep saying “someday.”

Someday when you have more time.
Someday when the timing is right.
Someday when everything is figured out.

But here’s the thing: your life is happening today. ❤️

Don’t wait so long to start living the life you want that you forget to enjoy the one you have.

What’s one thing you’re done putting off until “someday”? 👇

Elizabeth Gilbert's new paperback, All the Way to the River, is out today! 📚✨

So we're bringing back this conversation because there are some ideas that are just too good not to revisit.

I loved this conversation with Liz. She is full of wisdom, honesty, and reminders about trusting yourself and following what feels true.

Congratulations, Liz, go grab her new paperback! ❤️
Comment READ and I'll send you the full episode.

@elizabeth_gilbert_writer

Sometimes you don’t need more answers. You need to ask yourself better questions. 🧠✨

Take a few minutes today to slow down, get quiet, and check in with yourself.

You might be surprised by what comes up when you stop looking outside yourself for the answer.

Which question made you stop and think? 👇

Your morning routine might be sabotaging your productivity before your day even starts. 📱🧠

The second you open your phone, you’re letting other people’s priorities, notifications, and noise into your brain before you’ve had a chance to focus on your own.

Try this instead: give yourself a little time in the morning before you reach for your phone.

Protect your attention. Protect your energy. And start your day on your terms. ✨

Could you go phone-free for the first 30 minutes of your day? 👇

Outside of work? 😂

I like to dance, laugh, play, explore, and enjoy the heck out of this wild little life. 💃✨

Because building a meaningful business matters to me, but so does having a life I actually love living.

linkedin.about:
Mel Robbins is the creator and host of the award-winning The Mel Robbins Podcast, one of the most successful podcasts in the world, and a #1 New York Times bestselling author of The Let Them Theory. She's also the founder and CEO of the media production company 143 Studios. She has amassed 40 million followers online and is one of the most respected experts in mindset, life improvement, and behavior change. The Wall Street Journal calls her a “billion-view podcaster” and TIME Magazine says she gives millions of listeners around the globe “a reason to believe in themselves.”

Her books have been translated into 63 languages and include the #1 New York Times, #1 Amazon, #1 Audible, and #1 Sunday Times bestselling The Let Them Theory, which is the top selling book of 2025 according to Publisher’s Weekly, with 7 million copies sold within nine months of its release date. It is on pace to have the best non-fiction book launch of all time. She is also the author of the multimillion-copy-selling The 5 Second Rule, The High 5 Habit, and seven #1 audiobook releases on Audible.

USA Today calls Mel “a force to be reckoned with.” She is a global phenomenon in the publishing industry and podcasting. Her Boston-based media production company, 143 Studios, produces award-winning content, podcasts, events, audio series, online courses, journals, and books, along with professional development education forpartners likeStarbucks, Ulta Beauty, JP Morgan Chase, LinkedIn, Headspace, and Audible.

The Mel Robbins Podcast has won some of the most prestigious awards given to podcasts, including Webby, Signal Awards, and iHeart. It was also recognized as one of Apple Podcasts' Top Shared and Followed Shows of 2024 and 2023 and Spotify Top Global Shows of 2024. Notable accolades for Robbins include being named to Time 100 Most Influential Digital Voices of 2025, a Forbes 50 Over 50 Honoree, USA Today Top 5 Mindset & Performance Coaches in the World, and one of the fifty most influential influencers on The Hollywood Reporter’s Creator A-List in 2024.

Thanks for being here!

Learn more at melrobbins.com.

Reach my team:
Press inquiries: TeamMelRobbins@align-pr.com
Speaking inquiries: darrin@powellspeakers.com
Brand partnership inquiries: MelRobbinsTeam@unitedtalent.com

positions.description: Pure Genius Protein is unlike any other protein you’ve ever had. It’s a protein shot containing 23 grams of complete protein in a TSA-friendly 3.38 oz bottle designed for busy schedules, travel, long shifts, low appetite days, and everything in between. It tastes like juice and it’s not chalky or bloating. It’s only 100 calories, zero sugar, zero fat, shelf-stable, lactose- and gluten-free, with no artificial flavors or sweeteners.

143 means “I Love You” (one letter to say “I,” four letters to say “love,” and three letters to say “you.”) And it’s true! I’m loving my work: We’re on a mission to create quality content, inspiring experiences and essential tools to help you be the leader in your own life. 143 is my personal sign from the Universe - Mr. Rogers used it as his sign too, so know I’m in good company. And I'm also in good company working with our collaborative, courageous and creative team at 143 Studios.

education.description:
Before I reinvented my own career, I was one of CNN's most popular on-air commentators and opinion writers. I analyzed stories that intersected legal, ethical and human behavior issues. My provocative opinion pieces were read by millions of people on CNN.com. I covered cases that deeply impacted me, especially the murders of Trayvon Martin, Michael Brown, Tamir Rice, and Eric Garner.

I stand behind and fight for social justice. This job, along with my time as a criminal defense attorney at Legal Aid in New York City, fueled my desire to help people get the fair treatment they deserve.

posts.caption:
Here's how companies use Google Ads differently based on company size.

The big difference is that larger companies optimize for LTV, while smaller ones tend to optimize more for eyeballs.

Your customers don’t care about your five-step process. They care about being up and running by Friday. Give them a date and they’ll buy it. AI has made it easier than ever to deliver results, but most business owners still get lost explaining how they work. Let tools like our partners at HighLevel handle the process. Your job is to sell the destination.

#SmallBusiness #SalesTips #AIMarketing #HighLevel #NeilPatel

That tough question a client asked you last month? That's your next piece of content. AI handles the easy questions from memory and moves on. The specific ones, tied to a real industry, company size and situation, push it past what it knows. That's when it starts pulling from sources. Your experience is the part AI doesn't already have.

#ContentMarketing #AISearch #SEO #MarketingTips

Want to know the biggest growth lever in Google Ads?

Funny enough, it has nothing to do with the Google advertising platform.

In today's world, most marketers see it as being creative and first-party data.

Check out the results.

On the 14th of August, ChatGPT quietly updated how it responds to queries.

For a year, everyone in my industry, including me, told you to go and get mentioned on Reddit, post on YouTube and social media.

But a firm called Petra Labs that tracks every link ChatGPT cites found something new.

In August YouTube dropped 88%, Reddit 81%, TikTok 72%.

A cliff like that is not a coincidence.

Some people suspect it's connected to negotiations between Reddit and OpenAI about their partnership.

But OpenAI claims it's just a routine update for relevance and performance.

Either way that loss is someo

Prompt in. Content out. Publish. Next. I get it. It's fast and it's cheap. But from what we're seeing, the AI models doing the citing favor content written by people. Use AI to research, outline, and draft. Then have a real person write or heavily rewrite what goes live.

#AIContent #SEO #ContentStrategy #DigitalMarketing

Here's how marketers should spend their time in an automated Google Ads world.

Data from 707 marketers.

Last month Google added a report to Search Console that most business owners have never opened.

Let me show you what it says. And what it leaves out.

Open Search Console, click performance, there's a new section, Generative AI.

It shows you impressions. That's how many times one of your pages appeared inside an AI answer. An AI Overview, or AI Mode.

And it shows which pages.

Think of it like a billboard company calling to tell you how many cars drove past.

Useful. Now here's what it doesn't tell you.

It doesn't show clicks. Because most of the time, there aren't any.

And it doesn't tel

Your content doesn't get quoted as a whole. It gets quoted in pieces. That's why listicles and roundups earned almost 22% of all citations in our survey of 1,000 marketers. Headers that say exactly what the section covers. Bullets where one bullet equals one fact. Tables for anything with numbers. If a piece can't stand on its own, it doesn't get quoted.

#AISearch #SEO #ContentStrategy #AIMarketing
Which Google Ads automation delivers the most value?

It's not a new ad campaign. It's the list of customers who haven't been back in six months. One message to all of them. Almost nobody sends it. That list is the cheapest revenue you'll ever find, and it's already sitting in your system.

#CustomerRetention #MarketingAutomation #SmallBusiness #NeilPatel

You can have the best answer on the internet and still get skipped. AI isn't reading every word. It's hunting for one clear line it can quote and move on. If you make that line hard to find, AI moves on to a source that didn't. Good content still matters. It just has to be easy to extract.

#AIMarketing #ContentStrategy #SEO #NeilPatel

linkedin.about:
I’m the host at Netflix’s new show, "How to Get Rich," and the New York Times best-selling author of “I Will Teach You To Be Rich.” I’m also the Founder and CEO of IWT, where we host over 1 million readers/month on business, careers, negotiation, psychology, and money.

My family is from India and my parents immigrated to the States in the 1970’s. With four kids and one income, they couldn’t afford to send me to college so I built a system to apply to 60+ scholarships. I worked hard to earn a full ride to Stanford.

But when I got my first scholarship check, I invested it in the stock market…and immediately lost half my money. Oops.

That’s when I decided to learn how money really worked. I quickly realized most money advice was irrelevant for people like you and me:

❌ Most money advice is about restriction. 
❌ Money is too confusing. Where are you supposed to start? And who do you trust?
❌ Nobody was talking about money psychology.

Fast forward to today. What I believe now:

✅ I believe in asking $30,000 questions, not $3 questions. Buy all the lattes you want.
✅ There’s a limit to how much you can cut, but no limit to how much you can earn.
✅ Your Rich Life is yours. I consider it a tragedy to live a smaller life than you have to.

HOW CAN I WILL TEACH YOU TO BE RICH HELP YOU?

At IWT, we now have a worldwide community of people who want to create their Rich Lives, their way. Here you’ll find:

➡️ The best free advice on money. Everything from earning more to how to live your Rich Life.
➡️ Earnable, our signature digital program that has helped over 30,000 people to start a business.
➡️ Money Coaching Program, which has a vibrant community who want to get skilled at their finances.

Start living the life you’ve always wanted to. 

GET THE CONSCIOUS SPENDING PLAN:
📥 iwt.com/csp-linkedin

positions.description:
After receiving my first scholarship in high school, I invested it in the stock market and immediately lost 50%. That's when I decided to learn something about personal finance. Since then...

http://www.iwillteachyoutoberich.com hosts over 1,000,000 readers/month, where I help people automate their finances so they can get on with their lives.

I've been featured in media like the Today Show, New York Times, Wall Street Journal -- all because we *know* we need to learn personal finance, but none of us actually do it. In 2009, I published "I Will Teach You To Be Rich," which became an instant Amazon #1 best-seller and a New York Times bestseller.

I combine my experience in social influence and persuasion with personal finance to focus on the tactical and psychological aspects of behavioral change. 

Money is first. 

Next up...?

education.description:
We launched PBwiki (now called PBworks) in 2005, making it easy to create a powerful wiki for online collaboration.

I ran marketing and usability for PBwiki, which involves a focus on the user experience and viral marketing. I also handled strategic partnerships and managing support for a user base of millions of users.

Omidyar Network is a "mission-based investment group committed to fostering individual self-empowerment on a global scale" (it's Pierre Omidyar's organization to effect social change).

Previously, I consulted on social psychology here. Later, I sourced and evaluated investment opportunities.

Captology (Computers as Persuasive Technologies) involves the combination of technology and persuasion. 

I've been a researcher and director in the Lab, where I've created experimental methodologies, analyzed data, and communicated our findings to others.

More recently, I spoke about persuasive technology in places like Japan and around the Bay area.

Read more: http://captology.stanford.edu

Storm brought me on to help get everyone up to speed on how young people are using technology. What's this Web 2.0 thing? Why are social networks important (and are they really just a fad?). Are college kids afraid of being sued for downloading music? How do mobile phones fit into the picture?

I made presentations and brought in experts to share the viewpoints of my generation.

Now here's the corporate version: Focused on emerging Internet technologies & investment evaluation. Worked closely with entire firm to source and evaluate deals.

I worked first as an intern, then was hired to stay on as a consultant to the CEO.

My initial job was to devise a viral-marketing strategy for AuctionDrop. After that, I studied and recommended changes for the end-to-end customer experience.

I was Seth's first-ever intern. I managed this by cold-calling him and convincing him that I could do it.

Since then, Seth has realized the value of interns and continues to hire them even today.

We worked on the book Free Prize Inside, which became a New York Times bestseller (and a WSJ bestseller, too).

I met/interviewed Fortune 500 CEOs and other innovators across industries and organizations. 

I was also a member of the strategy team for political-marketing site, which used classic persuasion and viral-marketing elements.

Coursework included theoretical and applied persuasion, entrepreneurship, computer science, human-computer interaction research and design, psychology, and policy analysis of the impact of emerging technologies on society.

I wrote a comedy column and ran projects in social entrepreneurship, captology, personal finance, and religious studies.
I studied social influence and persuasion in a study-abroad tutorial, and ate horrible, horrible food. My papers are online at http://www.RamitSethi.com.

posts.caption:
You’re good at your job. Your friends are great. You like your life.

So why does dating feel like the one thing you can’t figure out?

Most people blame the apps, their schedule, or the idea that there just aren’t any good people left. But a lot of the time, the real problem is closer to home: how your week is set up, the habits that take over when dating feels uncertain, and whether your standards are protecting you or just keeping you from trying.

Next Wednesday, October 14 at 12pm ET / 9am PT, dating coach and matchmaker Blaine Anderson is joining Rich Life Expert Sessions to walk you thr

Still moving money between accounts every payday? You can set that up once and let it happen automatically.

My free Money Made Easy download shows you, step by step, how to split your paycheck between investments, savings, and bills—so everything goes where it needs to go automatically.

Comment START and I’ll DM you the link.

Already automated your money? What’s been the biggest relief?

These are my Money Rules.

If you had to create 3 Money Rules for yourself, what would they be? I love hearing your Money Rules!

By the way, I notice a funny thing: when people create their first rules, they’re almost always restrictive:

Don’t spend on ____
Never buy ____
Go for the generic ____

I’ll ask, “Does that rule excite you?”
They laugh. “Not really”

PICK EXCITING RULES!

Use my free Design Your Rich Life mini course so you can say YES to more. Comment “DESIGN” and I’ll send you a DM with the link.

A lot of you have asked me to set up I Will Teach You To Be Rich for single people who want to meet each other.

Here’s the next best thing.

On Wednesday at 12pm ET / 9am PT, dating coach and matchmaker Blaine Anderson (@datingbyblaine) is joining our next Expert Session. She’s helped thousands of people figure out what’s really getting in the way of their dating life, and she’s going to show you the reasons yours might not be working, plus the simple, practical changes you can make this week.

If you’re single, don’t miss this one. Comment DATING and I’ll send you the free link to register.

You can only cut so much.

Skip the lattes, cancel every subscription, cook every meal at home. At best, you free up a few hundred dollars a month. Then you hit the floor.

But there’s no ceiling on the other side.

Making an extra $500 a month on the side is the same as getting a $6,000 raise. An extra $1,000 a month is a $12,000 raise.

Most people never try because they think they need a brilliant idea, a lot of money, or to quit their job. You don’t. You need one idea people will pay for, and you’re probably already good at something that could become one.

Comment CHALLENGE and I’ll send

Here’s why you should pause before you make any of these moves:

Rushing to pay off a house
→ Now what? You have ongoing costs and sacrificed decades of investment gains so you could own a house “free and clear.”

Cashing out investments to pay debt
→ It feels so great to be debt-free! Except you lost decades of investment gains.

Partner quitting because childcare costs are high
→ Could be a very valid decision, but before you make this highly consequential move, did you carefully decide—together—which expenses you’ll cut? How about the ones that may grow? What about re-entry into the workfor

You can make $185,000 a year and still end up fighting over the prices at Target.

When there’s no plan, every purchase becomes a debate. Dinner out, a concert, a quick store run. But when you know your numbers, you don’t have to argue about each one. You already know the answer, yes or no. And sometimes the answer will be no. That’s part of having a plan.

Comment CSP and I’ll send you my free Conscious Spending Plan template to help you and your partner decide in advance what you’ll spend on, so you can stop fighting over every purchase.

▶️ Watch and listen to “Money For Couples” on Spotify

This commenter noticed something that happens on the podcast all the time.

When I even question private school, it’s an immediate no. Sometimes there are tears, even for couples who are drowning in debt.

I get it. No parent wants to feel like they’re shortchanging their kids.

But that reaction isn’t about the numbers. It’s an invisible script: “Good parents pay for private school.” And when something is off-limits before you’ve even looked at it, it’s not a decision anymore. It’s a rule someone else wrote for you.

Private school can be a great choice. It’s also one of the biggest Fixed Cos

I love meeting people in our community. When I ask what the most important parts of their Rich Life are, 99% of the time the answers are health, relationships, and career.

But when I follow up with, “What have you spent money on lately to invest in these things?”

Silence.

I always say, “Show me someone’s calendar and their spending, and I’ll show you their priorities.”

The fix is to get specific. “I want time and freedom” gives you nothing to work toward. “I want to spend a month in NYC every year” tells you exactly what to plan and save for.

Comment JOURNAL and I’ll send you the first ch

If you keep asking where the money for a trip is going to come from, the answer is usually that there was never a plan.

Avoiding that reality doesn’t make the money appear. It just pushes the disappointment down the road. The fix isn’t another vague conversation. It’s deciding ahead of time how much goes toward the things you care about, like travel.

Comment CSP and I’ll send you my free Conscious Spending Plan template so you can plan for the trips you want instead of hoping the money shows up.

▶️ Watch and listen to “Money For Couples” on Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcast

They’re in their early 30s. They’re maxing out their retirement accounts. And they’re investing even more on top of that.

Now they want to know: “Are we saving too much for retirement?”

I ran their numbers and told them exactly what I’d do.

Comment NEWSLETTER and I’ll send you the link to get my full breakdown in Saturday’s email.

Supporting your partner’s dream shouldn’t mean ignoring the numbers.

When you’re $633,000 to $1 million in debt with no retirement, this isn’t about long-term wealth anymore. It’s about protecting your family. And sometimes the most loving thing you can do is ask the hard question: When is it time to call it?

Comment MONEY TALK and I’ll send you my free guide on how to talk to your partner about money, including the conversations you’ve been putting off.

▶️ Watch and listen to “Money For Couples” on Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.

posts.caption:
✨🦄 NEW PR AT THE BOSTON MARATHON!!! 🦄✨

3:27:37
7:55/mile pace
Four minute PR from my best previous time at Berlin 2024

Honestly, still speechless over this. I cannot believe that at age 44, one week after a 100k race, five months post-injury…that this happened. An entire marathon at a mile pace that starts with a 7! A Boston Qualifying time AT BOSTON! And to do this with my son here with me! OMFG!!! 

Have been working so so hard, and it doesn’t always come together on race day. But when it does…there’s no feeling quite like it. 

Time to go eat all the food and cry so many happy tears.

Fastest Known Time on the Baja Sur 135km Trail! 

On March 6, I attempted the Fastest Known Time (FKT) for Mexico’s 135km Baja Sur Trail across the entire Baja Sur Peninsula. 

82 miles from the Pacific Ocean → Sea of Cortez.
13,000 feet of elevation.
One absolutely savage mountain section from miles 17–34 that climbed 6,000 feet in just 6 miles — including three straight miles at 30% grade in peak heat.
40 miles through night under the moon and stars.
One 5-minute dirt nap after mile 60.
And a sunrise at mile 70 that made the entire effort feel almost spiritual.

My first “comeback” ultra dis

Officially a @cocodona250 finisher.
Still processing the experience and will have a more in depth post soon, but for now: 

257 miles across Arizona
36,000+ feet of elevation
6 total hours of sleep across 5 days
Torrential rain, insane heat, snow, lightning & hail
Insane amounts of Coca Cola & cookies consumed
65 miles done on a busted shin/ankle
Hysterical laugher and full body crying 
Met my own soul (several times)
Literally the greatest friends on the planet
An accomplishment nobody can ever take from me

📷: @howiesternphoto @ekzooks

My ginormous baby is TWELVE today!!! 🥹🎂❤️

We are celebrating with a mother-son adventure in Chicago! A weekend of running, matching outfits, deep dish pizza, friends and birthday surprises. 

Happy birthday, Simi! I love watching you grow up, even if I wish you’d slow down just a tiny bit. (Vertically and literally)

We are officially an entire running family now. 

Today’s family scoreboard at the Run For Love 5k:

🏆 Asher WON THE ENTIRE RACE! 

🔥 Shira broke 10 MINUTES in the mile!!! 
Tiny legs, enormous swagger.

❤️ Dad paced Simi to glory for his entire 8 mile run and coached Shira with a last minute pep talk at the start line.

First place female and second fastest female time ever!

Miami, you were beautiful, painful, chaotic, insane and amazing in all the best ways. The race was an adventure-style checkpoint race, where you didn’t learn the course until you were in it, and you got the directions for each checkpoint in real time. I ran over bridges, around islands, through neighborhoods, and navigated crowded touristy areas. All in hot and crazy humid Florida weather.

I walked into OTF almost four years ago with no clue how that gym would change my life. Countless 6am classes, some of my closest friendships, big goals dreamt & done, and a whole lot of life lived under those orange lights. Naturally, we celebrated the only reasonable way: a 6am toga party. 

🔥 My son’s new 5k PR! I got to run side by side in matching outfits with my son Simi, as he dug so deep and set a new PR on the exact same course where he last set a PR at this distance, two years ago. Super proud mom.
